title: My Schedule
description: Describe a simple daily schedule with days and times.
objectives: Describe a simple daily schedule with days and times.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to describe a simple daily schedule with days and times. The central language is present simple with time expressions. It belongs to the practical context of numbers, time & dates. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.english: I work at nine on weekdays.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the my schedule exchange.

blocks.english: My English class is on Tuesday.
blocks.explanation: This my schedule model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the my schedule exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I work at nine on weekdays.” and “My English class is on Tuesday.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: present simple with time expressions.
